newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The first government meeting to shape the positions that will be put on the negotiating table during social dialogue between the government, unions and employers will be held today. The initial hardline stance by the government appears to be changing in the face of loud protests while latest reports say that bank and public organisation employees will receive wage increases of up to 10.0 percent.
--Athens and Rome appear to be at loggerheads over the details of the multinational protection force for Albania while the anti-Italian feeling continues to run high in the neighbouring country.
--Ten leading members of ruling party PASOK have called for an end to the squabbling between family members of late PASOK founder and president Andreas Papandreou.
--Alternate Foreign Minister George Papandreou explains why it is important to send Greek troops to Albania. Training of the troops is under way at the 71st Battalion's camp in Kilkis.
--New Democracy leader Costas Karamanlis returned to his constituency of Thessaloniki over the weekend, the first visit since his victory as party leader.
--Radars and radio assistance at 20 airports around the country are non-existent according to reports in Sunday's press, causing a massive headache for the transport and communications ministry.

--The finance ministry will begin cutbacks in overtime rates for civil servants in an effort to control spending on overtime which can exceed monthly pay bills. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
